rows.grounds: Compound describing the deity as possessing a tilaka mark on the forehead; continues the accusative description of the three-eyed form in the preceding verses.
Compound describing the deity as having radiance attached to or reflected in a mirror; continues the accusative description of the same form.

items.question: What forehead adornment and quality of radiance characterize the depicted three-eyed deity?
premises: The depicted deity is endowed with a mark on the forehead.
The depicted deity possesses radiance associated with a mirror.
These attributes further qualify the auspicious three-eyed form described previously.
items.inference: Therefore the deity's form is distinguished by a forehead tilaka and mirror-associated radiance.
uncertainties: The precise sense of darpaṇāsaktatejasam—whether radiance fixed on a mirror or radiance like that of a mirror—remains contextually ambiguous.
items.plain_english: He is adorned with a mark on his forehead and possesses a radiance associated with a mirror.
